rows.name: Hua Mochi Aloha
rows.notes: No own website, Instagram or Facebook found from permitted sources. A Feb 2026 blog post says they pop up at KCC Farmers Market on Saturdays and Mililani Farmers Market on Sundays. The Marketspread vendor page lists both markets. The Hawaii Farm Bureau (HFBF) archive says the business was formerly Daizu Tei. A Yelp listing suggests the handle hua_mochialoha, but I did not use it because it is a review site and the handle is unconfirmed. Home base is not stated, so side is null.

rows.name: Bueno Salsa
rows.notes: The HFBF Kailua and Mililani market pages list Bueno Salsa (Andy; handmade salsas and pickles; Kailua-grown ghost pepper recipes; contact email buenochalupa@hotmail.com). Marketspread also lists it under Mililani with a Kailua zip (96734). No own website, Instagram or Facebook found, so those are null. The HFBF Kailua page shows the vendor at the Kailua market (Thursdays).

rows.name: Burgers & Burritos Hawaii (BBHI)
rows.notes: The HFBF Mililani page lists BBHI (Chef Jonathan) and gives the website and the email beyondburgers@gmail.com. A 2017 student-paper article gave a Kapahulu Ave restaurant address. I could not verify whether that restaurant is still open, so still_active reflects the current Mililani market listing only. I did not open the website, so its content is unchecked. Marketspread lists the legal name as Beyond Burgers Hawaii LLC dba Burgers & Burritos Hawaii (Honolulu 96826). No Instagram or Facebook handle was found. Side 'town' is not set because the base is only inferred from the older address.

rows.name: Ed's Little Farm
rows.notes: The farm's own site says it is family-owned, in Waialua on the North Shore. It lists Kakaʻako Farmers Market on Saturdays 8am-12pm and Mililani Farmers Market 8am-11am. The HFBF page lists more markets: Mililani on Sunday, Honolulu (Blaisdell) on Wednesday, Kailua on Thursday and KCC on Saturday. No Instagram or Facebook found.

rows.name: Grandma G's Ono Grindz
rows.notes: The business's own site names the Instagram handle @grandmagsonogrindz. Its locations page lists Sunday 8-11am at Mililani High School and Thursday 4-7pm at Kailua Town Center. A Sept 2026 blog post says they were back at Mililani and to follow the same handle for locations. A third-party directory mentions a Facebook page but gave no URL, so Facebook is null. The only address found is a mailing address, so side is null.

rows.name: Green & Fit Mama
rows.notes: The HFBF Mililani page lists the vendor with website www.greenandfitmama.com and email greenandfitmama@gmail.com. The Facebook page shows the same email. The owner's own site says the Raw Superfood Bars are sold at weekend farmers markets on Oʻahu and at Down to Earth stores. The site now also features wellness topicals and a Fit Moms Club. A blog post says the business has an Instagram account but gives no handle, so Instagram is null. A public LinkedIn profile for the owner gives Mililani Town, hence side central. No dedicated schedule page found.

rows.name: Thai Farmers Association
rows.notes: Listed on the current HFBF Mililani page (assorted produce, free-range organic chicken eggs). Marketspread describes a 10-acre farm in Kunia and lists KCC and Mililani. No own website or social accounts found. Kunia is not clearly central or Ewa, so side is null.

rows.name: Grok Coffee
rows.notes: The own website's beans page lists free pickup at Kakaʻako Farmers Market on Saturdays and Mililani Farmers Market on Sundays, and shows ordering by the ounce. The Facebook page text mentions weekly Kakaʻako and Mililani market stops. The website says it follows Grok Coffee on Instagram but gives no handle in the results, so Instagram is null. The business is based at 2444 Jasmine St, Honolulu 96816. Coffee comes from Hawaiʻi roasters; I did not verify the 'local syrups' claim.

rows.name: Kalihi Corner
rows.notes: Only the HFBF Mililani market page was found. It lists plate lunches (shoyu chicken, short rib stew, stuffed salmon puffed pastries) and the email kalihicornerllc@gmail.com. No own website, Instagram or Facebook found. Base location is not stated, so side is null.

rows.name: Okonokai
rows.notes: The own website sells Sea Crackers and dried limu made with Kona-grown seaweed. The Instagram bio (@okonokai, 'Okonokai Sea Snacks') matches the products. A business directory lists the company as Honolulu-based (Limu Labs LLC, founder Jina Wye). I did not confirm a Mililani market listing from an organizer page. The website FAQ's retailer list under an 'OAHU' heading shows only Hawaiʻi Island stores. No schedule page found, and no Facebook found. Base is only given as Honolulu, so side is null.

rows.name: Sally's Farm
rows.notes: The HFBF pages give the Instagram handle @sallysfarm808 and list KCC (Saturday) and Mililani (Sunday). The Facebook page uses the same handle but shows its location as 'Kahuku', whereas Marketspread says Kahaluu and another vendor page says Kaneohe, so Facebook is lower certainty. The KCC page was current about 73 days before this search. sallysfarm.com is an unrelated farm in Thailand and was excluded, so website is null.

rows.name: Small Kine Farm
rows.notes: The Facebook page lists smallkinefarm.com and the email smallkinefarm@gmail.com. A MidWeek article also cites smallkinefarm.com. The HFBF page is older and says Mililani on the 1st, 3rd and 5th Sundays, plus Kailua and KCC. The current HFBF Mililani page still lists the farm. A third-party source mentions an online store but I did not confirm its URL, so order_url is null. No Instagram found.

rows.name: Son Farm
rows.notes: Only the HFBF Mililani page was found (small family farm in Pearl City selling watercress, taro, onions, eggplant, cucumbers, bell peppers, choi sum). No own website or social accounts found. Do not confuse it with Sumida Farm, the watercress farm in Pearl City. Pearl City is placed under leeward_ewa, which is a judgment call.

rows.name: Once Again
rows.notes: The business is Once Again Hawaii, a family-owned succulent nursery in Waimanalo. Its own site has a 'Pop-Ups + Locations' section and gives the farm address 41-829 Kakaina St. The HFBF Mililani page describes repurposed vessels (spam cans, eggshells, teacups) and lists onceagainhawaii@gmail.com and the website. No Instagram or Facebook found.

rows.name: Da Tomato Guy
rows.notes: The search for this vendor failed, so I found nothing on it. I did not guess any handles or URLs. It should be checked on the HFBF Mililani and Honolulu market pages.
